name: Ischgl
kurzbeschreibung: The beating heart of the Paznauntal – legendary Après-Ski parties, world-class concerts, and 239 kilometers of ski runs.
beschreibung:
Overview

Ischgl is situated at an elevation of 1,377 metres in the Paznaun Valley in southwestern Tyrol, within the district of Landeck. Nestled between the monumental three-thousand-metre peaks of the Silvretta to the south and the Verwall Alps to the north, the village has around 1,640 inhabitants. Spreading along the Trisanna River, Ischgl has evolved from a secluded farming hamlet into one of the most prestigious winter sports and lifestyle capitals of the Alps. Together with the Swiss duty-free enclave of Samnaun, the cross-border Silvretta Arena boasts 239 kilometres of groomed slopes rising up to 2,872 metres at Greitspitz. Beyond world-class skiing, Ischgl is celebrated for luxury hospitality, gourmet dining, and its iconic Top of the Mountain Concerts on the Idalp. In summer, the mountain village shifts into an expansive alpine playground for hikers, mountaineers, and mountain bikers.

History

The name Ischgl stems from the Rhaeto-Romanic word iscla, meaning an island or alluvial meadow. From the 10th century onwards, Rhaeto-Romanic settlers from Switzerland's Lower Engadine crossed high mountain passes such as the Fimber Pass to colonize the valley. The earliest documented mention dates to 1427 as Yschkl in a Tyrolean tax register. For centuries, the parish belonged ecclesiastically to the Bishopric of Chur in Graubünden. Harsh alpine poverty compelled many villagers during the 18th and 19th centuries to seek seasonal agricultural work in southern Germany. The turning point arrived with the construction of the Paznaun federal road in the 1880s and the founding of the tourist association in 1929. The founding of Silvrettaseilbahn AG in 1961 and the opening of the Idalp cable car in 1963 laid the cornerstone for modern tourism, culminating in the 1979 ski union with Samnaun. The architectural pride of the village is the Baroque Parish Church of St. Nicholas, rebuilt in 1755–1757 with Rococo stuccowork.

Getting There

Ischgl enjoys reliable transportation infrastructure. Drivers take the Inntal Motorway A12 or Arlberg Expressway S16 to the Pians/Paznaun exit, following the federal road B188 for 30 kilometres past See and Kappl directly into Ischgl. In summer, the scenic Silvretta High Alpine Road across the Bielerhöhe pass (2,037 m) provides toll access from Vorarlberg. Rail passengers travel on international Railjet or Eurocity services to Landeck-Zams station. From the station terminal, regional bus line 260 runs frequently throughout the day directly into Ischgl, allowing seamless car-free travel.

Tips

In winter, exploring the Silvretta Arena is an unparalleled experience, including the famous cross-border Smuggler's Circuits and riding the double-decker Twinliner cable car into Samnaun for duty-free shopping. Wellness seekers shouldn't miss the Silvretta Therme Ischgl, an architectural masterpiece opened in 2022 featuring thermal pools, panoramic saunas, and a rooftop ice-skating track. In summer, hike the "Walk of Lyrics" across two vertigo-inducing suspension bridges spanning the Kitzloch and Flim gorges up to Idalp, or soar down the canyon on the Ischgl Skyfly zipline at speeds of up to 85 km/h.
